body:
The session added canvas, the driver's sixteenth verb and twelfth instance verb, after layout: a read of the draw commands an app's widget paints into a canvas element, as a summary (command counts by kind and a digest) or a full dump of one closed line per command, paged in parts within the answer budget.
The verb rides every carrier: the session socket, the escher-session command line (canvas --id, --full, --part), the MCP tool canvas listed after layout with help last, and a kept check whose tool is canvas; Session::canvas reads in process too and opens no span of its own.
No new refusal cause, session error, exit status, node key, argument kind or span field; the command span records verb alone for canvas and, refused, verb and cause; the tool_call span records tool and ending and parents one command.
No canvas answer, MCP result or kept check holds a glyph id, a glyph position, text, a font's bytes or a family name; host_log and mcp_log read 0 canvas needles at trace.
Measured: the Cells actions answer 118,292 to 130,496 bytes for 678 nodes; target verbs per listed actions node five to six; stand_act_spans calls per mode 41 to 43; a 100-circle dump in 6 parts each within 10,000 bytes; CI green on linux, windows and macOS.
The engine gained a read of one custom widget's scene outside a raster, and the cold-agent pipe's verb list takes canvas while its counted verbs stay unchanged.

body_fields.rule: The cold-agent pipe lists canvas among its verbs but counts none of its calls, and the verdict holds no canvas counter until a served app holds a canvas.
body_fields.why: No app the pipe serves holds a canvas yet.
body_fields.because: The pipe's verb list took canvas while its counted verbs stayed unchanged, a chosen limit the verdict rows must not be read past.

body_fields.why: A canvas's content no longer crosses only as shot pixels: the canvas verb carries its draw commands as closed words, numbers and digests on the socket, the command line, MCP and a kept check.
body_fields.because: The chunk adds the canvas verb on every carrier, so the row's name, rule and key, all built on pixels alone, are false and an heir states the widened crossing.

body_fields.name: Canvas content crossing
body_fields.rule: A canvas's app-painted content crosses as pixels in a shot and, on the socket, the command line, MCP and a kept check, as a canvas answer of closed words, numbers and 64-bit digests, fonts and images as indexes with digests, never a glyph id, glyph position, text, font bytes or family name.
body_fields.because: The canvas verb carries a canvas's draw commands on every ratified carrier as closed values and digests, replacing the pixels-only crossing.

body_fields.name: Cold-agent runs carry canvas answers to the provider
body_fields.rule: The cold-agent pipe's call allowlist takes the canvas verb, so a live run carries canvas answers through the claude client to the model provider.
body_fields.because: The cold-agent pipe's allowlist takes canvas, and the standing provider row cannot take the canvas answer within its bound.

body_fields.value: A list of entries each holding verb, a word of the verb table, and cause, a closed cause word left out when absent; every listed node carries layout with no cause, and canvas with no cause on an app that can paint text.
body_fields.because: The actions answer now lists canvas among each node's target verbs, with no cause where the app can paint text.

body_fields.value: One of the twelve instance verbs.
body_fields.because: The instance verbs moved from eleven to twelve with canvas, and a kept check's tool may name it.

body_fields.value: Time on a held instance moves only when a caller asks for it with advance, 1 to 60000 ms a call; no driver verb has an argument or result field of a wait, and snapshot, screenshot, lint, graph, actions and canvas wait on no load.
body_fields.because: The canvas read moves no clock and leaves timer ticks unapplied, so it joins the verbs that wait on no load.

body_fields.value: No driver call or in-process read puts screen content in a log: typed text, element ids, accessible names, a shot's image, lint findings, a part's text, a UI graph, an actions answer, a layout answer, a canvas answer, a coverage check and a step's caused text reach no log line at any level.
body_fields.because: No canvas answer content reaches the host or MCP role log at trace, so the canvas answer joins the content kept out of logs.

body_fields.value: Records the instance-level verb; a graph call, a graph part's included, an actions, layout or canvas call records the verb alone, plus cause when refused, never the part asked or the part count.
body_fields.because: The command span records the canvas verb alone and, refused, its cause.

body_fields.promise: Takes a required id within the id bound, an optional full flag and an optional part from 1 to 1000; any other argument, full twice, or part 0 or 1001 is refused malformed with nothing run, and the verb adds no cause, argument kind, session error or exit status.
body_fields.because: The chunk adds the canvas verb as a new external-input surface validated by the closed schema, and its argument contract stands nowhere.

body_fields.name: Canvas read on a session changes nothing
body_fields.rule: The session's canvas read, in process or through the canvas verb on any ratified carrier, refuses an unknown id as not-found or stale and an app that cannot paint text as fonts-unavailable, and moves no snapshot, focus reading, diff or virtual clock, leaving timer ticks unapplied.
body_fields.because: The new canvas read is a read-only verb with its own refusals, which no standing row states.

body_fields.name: canvas
body_fields.because: The chunk occupies canvas as the driver verb and the MCP tool name.

body_fields.promise: Bare, taking no value.
body_fields.because: The escher-session command line gains the bare --full flag of the canvas command.

body_fields.name: Kept check holds the canvas answer
body_fields.rule: A kept check holds a canvas step and its whole answer of closed words, numbers and 64-bit digests, never a glyph id, text or NodeId, and its replay stops naming digest when a canvas digest differs.
body_fields.because: A kept check now records canvas calls whole, a new content class beside the layout, graph and actions answers it keeps.

body_fields.name: The canvas dump is paged
body_fields.rule: The canvas summary is unpaged; a full dump over the 10,000-byte text budget is cut into parts of whole lines each within it, the font and image indexes in part 1 alone and a part past the last empty.
body_fields.because: The canvas answer adds a paged dump under the answer budget, applied on a delegate's word ahead of its ratification.

body_fields.value: A screenshot, lint or canvas on an app with no usable font is refused fonts-unavailable with nothing changed.
body_fields.because: Session::canvas is refused fonts-unavailable where the app cannot paint text, so the row's list of verbs so refused must name canvas.

body_fields.value: tools/list offers the sixteen verbs in order, `layout` after `actions`, `canvas` after `layout` and `help` last.
body_fields.because: The MCP tool listing moved from fifteen to sixteen with `canvas` after `layout`, so the stated count and order are false.

body_fields.value: A step holds `tool` among the sixteen driver verbs, `arguments` an object and `expect` a list of strings; a check holds at most 400 steps.
body_fields.because: The cold-agent pipe's verb list takes canvas and moved from fifteen to sixteen, so a step's tool is one of sixteen verbs.

body_fields.value: True when the init tools are exactly the sixteen `mcp__escher__{verb}` tools, one MCP server `escher` is connected, skills and slash commands are empty, the API key source is none and no `cwd` or `memory_paths` names the repository root's basename.
body_fields.because: The MCP server now lists sixteen tools and the pipe reads sixteen, so the isolation check's tool count of fifteen is false.

body_fields.value: The session socket carries a call's element id and typed text in, and ids, accessible names, control values (a password's or file input's as the fixed mask), the snapshot's text, the diff, a step's caused with its error text, lint findings, layout answers and canvas answers out.
body_fields.because: The canvas verb is served over the session socket's call, so canvas answers now cross it outward and the list of what crosses is incomplete.

body_fields.value: `snapshot`, `screenshot`, `lint`, `graph`, `layout` and `canvas` run no step and wait on nothing.
body_fields.because: The canvas verb is a new reading verb that runs no step and waits on no load, so the closed list of reading verbs must name it.

body_fields.value: `escher-session <verb> … --session <dir>` is the whole command line, sixteen verbs; the instance-level verbs take their arguments as flags spelt as the schema spells them (`--id`, `--text`, `--key`, `--ms` and `--part` each with one value, `--shift`, `--ctrl` and `--full` bare).
body_fields.because: The command line gains the canvas command with a bare `--full` flag and the verb count moved from fifteen to sixteen.

body_fields.value: Sixteen verbs in a stated order at three levels — `instance`, `session`, `tool` — each with help, arguments and at least one result field.
body_fields.because: The verb table moved from fifteen to sixteen verbs with canvas after layout, so the stated count is false.

body_fields.value: A password typed through the driver and a file input's path occur nowhere in what a call returns, graph, actions, layout and canvas answers included, nor in a kept or an explored path's check, in both layout modes; the value reads the mask, and a typed password never leaves as pixels.
body_fields.because: The masks check now reads the new canvas answer for the typed sentinel and the file input, so the answers the rule covers include canvas.

body_fields.value: `tools/list` offers the sixteen verbs in order, `graph` after `lint`, `actions` after `graph`, `layout` after `actions`, `canvas` after `layout` and `help` last.
body_fields.because: The MCP tool listing moved from fifteen to sixteen with `canvas` after `layout`, so the stated count and order are false.

body_fields.name: Canvas commands held to one table across hosts
body_fields.rule: Circle Drawer's canvas draw commands are read in process in both layout modes into one committed table, at boot, after a click and at 12 and 100 circles, as summary, full dump and parts, each answer held equal by size and digest on linux x86_64, windows x86_64 and macOS aarch64.
body_fields.because: The chunk adds a cross-host committed table for canvas command reads, a test strategy no standing row states, the shot rows covering pixels alone.

body_fields.promise: Answers a summary by default (command counts per kind, size, digest), the whole dump with `full`, or one part with `part` 1 to 1000; an element holding no canvas reads `canvas` false; an unread or deleted id is refused `not-found` or `stale`, changing nothing.
body_fields.because: The canvas verb is a new reading of the driver session whose answer levels and refusals no row states.

body_fields.name: Canvas answer holds no content
body_fields.rule: A canvas answer holds closed words, numbers and 64-bit digests only, never a glyph id, a glyph position, text, font bytes or a family name, on every carrier and in kept checks.
body_fields.because: The canvas answer is a new surface crossing socket, command line, MCP and kept checks, and what it may hold is a boundary decision no row states.

body_fields.promise: A canvas read is deterministic: two reads give the same bytes, a click's line diff is all added and none removed, and an advance with nothing drawn reads an empty diff.
body_fields.because: The canvas read is promised diffable and repeatable, a contract of the new verb no row states.

body_fields.promise: A canvas dump over the text budget is cut into parts of whole lines, each within 10,000 bytes, fonts and images in part 1 alone; the parts joined equal the whole, and a part past the last is empty.
body_fields.because: The canvas dump is paged by its own cut, a contract beside the snapshot's and graph's parts that no row states.

body_fields.promise: A canvas command has no identity: a changed command reads as one line removed and one added, until virtual nodes give commands an identity.
body_fields.because: The chunk ships a stated limit of the canvas diff that checks and future work must read as a promise of the answer.

body_fields.promise: A layer's filter is written as a flag only.
body_fields.because: The chunk ships a stated limit of the canvas line form, what a layer's filter reads as, which no row states.

body_fields.promise: `canvas --id <id> [--full] [--part <part>]` takes `--part` as a whole number 1 to 1000 and `--full` once, anything else refused `malformed`, status `1`; an accepted answer is one line, status `0`.
body_fields.because: The usage line gains the canvas command, which would pass the usage row's bound, so the command's form stands as a row of its own.

body_fields.name: Control edit leaves earlier test targets green
body_fields.rule: A control whose case lies in the later of two test targets named by one gate entry with no fail-fast override needs an edit that leaves the earlier target green.
body_fields.why: Cargo runs the targets in name order and stops at the first red one, so the named case would go unrun.
body_fields.because: The chunk measured that a control reddening an earlier target leaves its own case unrun, a rule for building controls no row states.

body_fields.fact: Circle Drawer's canvas commands are read in process in both layout modes as one committed table of 17 rows (boot, after a click, 12 and 100 circles; summary, full and parts), held equal by size and digest on linux, windows x86_64 and macOS aarch64.

The canvas verb answers a summary by default (command counts per kind, size, digest), the whole dump with full, or one part with part 1 to 1000; an element holding no canvas reads canvas false; an unread or deleted id is refused not-found or stale, changing nothing.
A canvas answer holds closed words, numbers and 64-bit digests only - never a glyph id, glyph position, text, font bytes or family name - on every carrier and in kept checks.
A canvas read is deterministic: two reads give the same bytes, a click's line diff is all added and none removed, and advance with nothing drawn reads an empty diff.
A canvas dump over the text budget is cut into parts of whole lines each within 10,000 bytes, fonts and images in part 1 alone, the parts joined equal to the whole, a part past the last empty.
A canvas command has no identity: a changed command reads as one line removed and one added until virtual nodes give commands an identity, and a layer's filter is written as a flag only.

A control whose case lies in the later of two --test targets of one entry with no --no-fail-fast needs an edit that leaves the earlier target green, since cargo runs targets in name order and stops at the first red one.
